this_experiment_findings.title: Receiver leg acts on a toggle decision made at dispatch time, unlike the webhook leg's per-delivery recheck
this_experiment_findings.problem: The webhook carve-out re-resolves the acting reviewer's `stamphog_review_inbox_prs` toggle on every delivery, so a mid-PR switch off stops new runs (Case 3). The receiver leg checks the toggle once, in review_hog's save-path receiver, then hands off to `process_inbox_pr_review`, which never re-checks. If the toggle flips off while the task waits in a broker backlog, the review still runs and posts a real GitHub approval for a reviewer who opted out before it executed. The window is the queue delay, so the exposure is small, but the two legs now answer the same gate question at different times for the same privileged outcome.
this_experiment_findings.suggestion: At the start of `process_inbox_pr_review`, re-resolve the gate through the registered hook (`get_inbox_acting_reviewer_resolver()`), the same fail-closed check the webhook carve-out uses. The task already holds `team_id` and `signal_report_id`; `task_created_by_id` would need one TaskRun lookup, or the resolver signature can grow an overload that re-derives it. When the recheck returns None, log and return before any GitHub or DB work.
this_experiment_findings.match_reason: Same claim and anchor (tasks.py:1109-1127): process_inbox_pr_review never re-checks the acting reviewer's toggle, trusting the queue-time decision unlike the webhook leg.

fresh_votes.evidence:
It is true that the task does not re-check the toggle. `process_inbox_pr_review` (products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1110-1200) never reads the toggle again. It trusts the check that review_hog's receiver ran on the save path (products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:126, which calls `_start_stamphog_review` via on_commit, then `queue_inbox_pr_review`). The docstring at tasks.py:1115-1117 says so.

The claim that this differs from the webhook path does not hold:
- The webhook carve-out also checks the toggle only once, when the delivery is processed (`_inbox_rereview_carve_out`, tasks.py:201-204, through `resolve_stamphog_acting_reviewer` at receivers.py:147-160).
- After that check, both paths do the same thing. They create a ReviewRun with `output["inbox_review"]` provenance and start the Temporal workflow on commit.
- The workflow and its activities never re-check the toggle. They only read `inbox_review` provenance (products/stamphog/backend/temporal/activities.py:175, 237, 451).
- On both paths, the gap between the toggle check and the posted approval is mostly the sandbox review itself, which takes minutes. On the inbox path the Celery queue delay adds only a little.

So both paths answer the gate question once, before the long step. Neither re-checks before posting, and the gap the finding points at is small next to that shared one.

AGENTS.md (products/stamphog/AGENTS.md ~100-110) only promises that switching the toggle off "stops new runs". A run that was already dispatched is effectively in flight on either path, and the dismissal rules still apply. Posting an approval only needs a toggle flipped in a seconds-wide window after a TaskRun save, which is an unlikely race.
fresh_votes.refutation:
This is not a real gap between the two paths. The webhook carve-out (tasks.py:201-204) also checks the toggle once, before it creates the run. From there both paths go through the same Temporal workflow, and that workflow never re-checks the toggle before posting the approval (activities.py:175/237/451 only read the `inbox_review` provenance).

The inbox path's extra window is only the Celery queue delay, and each path already has the longer sandbox run between check and approval. Neither path re-checks there, so this does not break the documented "stops new runs" rule.

Adding a re-check at the start of the task would not close the larger gap. Triggering the issue needs someone to flip the toggle within a few seconds of the dispatch, which is too unlikely to count as a defect.

fresh_votes.evidence: The receiver leg does check the toggle once, when the TaskRun output is saved (products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:126). It then queues `process_inbox_pr_review` on commit (receivers.py:131-139), and that task never checks the toggle again (products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1109-1200). The webhook leg's check has the same shape. `_resolve_inbox_carve_out` calls the resolver once per delivery (tasks.py:201-205), stamps provenance, and creates the run with `transaction.on_commit(_start_review_workflow)` (tasks.py:1064-1073). Neither leg checks the toggle again during the Temporal review workflow. That workflow runs a sandbox and an LLM, so it takes minutes, and the GitHub review is posted at its end. A toggle switched off in that window still gets an approval posted on either leg.
fresh_votes.refutation: The claim that the two legs answer the gate question "at different times" does not hold up in any way that matters. Both legs check once and then act later without checking again. The receiver leg adds only the Celery broker delay (normally seconds). That is small next to the multi-minute review workflow that follows on both legs, and the proposed fix would not cover that workflow. The trigger needs the acting reviewer to switch the toggle off in the seconds between the implementation run saving its PR URL and the Celery task being picked up. That is a speculative race with no realistic trigger. The approval is the Stamphog App's review, which the reviewer opted into, not a credential the user owns. Existing safety still applies: on later head changes, a toggle that is off routes to the skip path, and that path dismisses the stale approval (tasks.py:161-165 docstring). The finding's own entry already carries is_valid=false.

fresh_votes.evidence: The code does what the finding says. `process_inbox_pr_review` (products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1110-1240) never re-checks `stamphog_review_inbox_prs`. The only check happens at dispatch, in review_hog/backend/receivers.py:126, inside a `transaction.on_commit` enqueue. The webhook path re-checks through the resolver inside the Celery task (tasks.py:201-204).
fresh_votes.refutation: The window the finding describes is not a real gap in production. (1) The trigger needs the acting reviewer to turn the toggle off in the gap between the TaskRun output save and the Celery worker picking up the task. With a healthy broker that is seconds, and the PR in question was opened moments earlier under their opt-in. (2) The webhook path has the same kind of gap, only longer. It checks the toggle once in the Celery task (tasks.py:201-204), then creates the ReviewRun and starts a Temporal workflow (tasks.py:1073). The sandbox and LLM review runs for minutes after that and never re-checks before posting the approval. So a recheck at the start of `process_inbox_pr_review` would not make the two paths equivalent at approval time. It would trim seconds off a window that is already minutes long in both paths. (3) The docstring at tasks.py:160-164 names the actual safety guarantee: once the toggle is off, head-changing deliveries retract the stale approval ("safety is never preference-gated"). The remaining consequence is one approval on a bot-authored draft that the user opted into seconds before. (4) The retry countdowns (tasks.py:1150-1155) stretch the delay only while GitHub is rate-limited or failing. That makes an already unlikely coincidence a little wider, not reachable in normal use. This is a speculative race with no practical trigger, and the finding's own validator marked it is_valid=false.

this_experiment_findings.title: Initial Stamphog review never re-checks the toggle at run time, so a mid-flight opt-out still mints a GitHub approval
this_experiment_findings.problem: The initial review leg checks `stamphog_review_inbox_prs` only once, in the TaskRun-save receiver, and `queue_inbox_pr_review` only publishes to Celery. The consuming task (`process_inbox_pr_review`) re-reads the repo config, fetches the PR from GitHub, and creates the run, but never re-checks the toggle, and it retries up to 3 times with countdowns that can exceed 60 seconds on rate limits. So a user who flips the toggle off right after the PR opens (or while the task sits in a retry loop) still gets the full review and a real GitHub approval posted on the draft head, and per the stated design that approval then takes effect when the draft flips to ready. This is inconsistent with the webhook re-review leg, which re-resolves the toggle through `resolve_stamphog_acting_reviewer` on every single delivery before doing anything. The whole point of the toggle is consent for automatic approvals, so consent withdrawn between queueing and execution should stop the run.
this_experiment_findings.suggestion: Re-check the toggle inside the queued task before creating the ReviewRun: resolve the acting reviewer through the registered `get_inbox_acting_reviewer_resolver()` hook (already available on that import path) and bail out when it returns None. That makes both legs enforce the same check-at-execution-time semantics and shrinks the opt-out window to zero.
this_experiment_findings.match_reason: Same claim and anchor (receivers.py:126): the receiver leg checks the toggle once at queue time and process_inbox_pr_review never re-validates it at execution.

fresh_votes.evidence: Premise traced end to end and confirmed. The consuming Celery task `process_inbox_pr_review` (products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1109-1240) resolves the repo config, fetches the PR, dedupes on head, creates the ReviewRun and starts the workflow; `acting_user_id` is only stamped into `output["inbox_review"]` (tasks.py:1181-1186), never re-validated. `grep stamphog_review_inbox_prs|acting_reviewer` over products/stamphog/backend/temporal and services hits only activities.py:175/237/451, all of which use `inbox_review` for analytics attribution and to skip the author merged-PR fetch, not consent. fresh_votes.refutation: Attempted refutations: (1) The single check is documented intent, not an oversight: tasks.py:1115-1116 says the task fires "after review_hog's TaskRun receiver resolved the acting reviewer and confirmed their toggle", and the carve-out docstring (tasks.py:160-165) explicitly addresses a toggle "switched off mid-PR" by relying on the skip path's stale-approval dismissal ("safety is never preference-gated"). So a post-opt-out approval is retracted on the next push; only the no-push ready-for-review flip on an unchanged head leaves the approval standing. Net: the defect is real (toggle not re-read at execution, inconsistent with the webhook leg), but it is bounded by the later-push retraction, documented as the leg's design, and the proposed fix is a cheap consistency hardening rather than a must-ship correctness fix. The reviewer's should_fix overstates it; the validator's `consider` is the right level.

this_experiment_findings.title: Re-check the opt-in toggle before creating the initial review
this_experiment_findings.problem: The task trusts the acting_user_id and creates the review without checking whether that user's stamphog_review_inbox_prs toggle is still enabled. The receiver checks the toggle before queueing, but Celery can run later, after the user opts out. This can start a review after the user disabled the feature.
this_experiment_findings.suggestion: Resolve the current acting reviewer and toggle again before building inbox_review or creating the ReviewRun.
